nodes.title: Staging sets VP_SAFETY_JUDGE_MODE=off alongside VP_LLM_DEFAULT_*, because both judges fall back to the default model (judge.ts judgeConfigured: VP_LLM_SAFETY_JUDGE_* ?? VP_LLM_DEFAULT_*; judge.py config: ... or ...) and default to shadow, so leaving VP_LLM_SAFETY_JUDGE_* unset no longer keeps the judge uncalled. Off keeps staging's judge exactly as before the fix: no judge calls, no judge events (verified: runtime runs False, control plane mode off, 0 judge events on the verification call)
nodes.rationale: The coordinator's brief wanted every VP_LLM_SAFETY_JUDGE_* unset 'because the judge stays shadow and unconfigured on staging'. With VP_LLM_DEFAULT_* set, unset alone would have run the judge in shadow on lab-gpt41mini-in (a model judge.json does not recommend) on every caller turn of calls, chats, simulations and analyses, with spend and judge marks on the owner's call pages.
nodes.reverse_if: The safety builder or the owner wants the judge measured or shown on staging: then configure VP_LLM_SAFETY_JUDGE_* on its recommended route (Flash-Lite on Vertex) and set the mode deliberately, or drop the line to accept shadow on the default model. Also reverse if the product stops falling back from the judge's purpose to VP_LLM_DEFAULT_*.

nodes.title: With a model configured, the AI-honesty brief review (here lab-gpt41mini-in through VP_LLM_DEFAULT_*, not its recommended route) flags the insurance-renewal template's own persona.notes[0] ('explain premiums like a friend who works in insurance') as a human persona (ai_honesty, kind human, confidence 0.9, 'publish: blocked until fixed'), so a buyer's first version.publish from that template is refused until the note is edited (staging, n = 1 review)
nodes.mitigation: Either reword the template note so it cannot read as a human persona, or route the brief review to its recommended model (VP_LLM_BRIEF_REVIEW_*) and re-check its false positives (BLIND-BR2 recorded false positives failing). Until then, tell the owner the renewal template needs that one note edited before publishing on staging.
